_comment: Synthetic fixture for the CStrArray vocabulary type. Mirrors the layout juliac would emit for `struct CStrArray; length::Int64; data::Ptr{CString}; owned::Int32; end` (JLWInterop), with one @ccallable function borrowing a CStrArray argument and one returning an owned one, plus the macro-emitted `jlw_free`/`jlw_free_strings` release entrypoints so the owning return is `:auto`, not `:mechanical`. `data` points to length-prefixed `CString` elements (`struct CString; length::Int32; data::Ptr{UInt8}; end`, size 16, offsets 0/8) rather than NUL-terminated `Ptr{UInt8}`s. The `owned::Int32` field at offset 16 (size 24 total, with 4 bytes of trailing padding) is the explicit ownership discriminant: 0 = caller-owned/borrowed, 1 = allocated by CStrArray's owning constructor. The Python emitter's façade free-on-return wrapper is gated on `_result.owned == 1`, never on call direction. The `Ptr{Nothing}`/synthetic zero-size `Nothing` struct for `jlw_free`'s void return mirrors juliac's actual ABI JSON rendering for that type verbatim. The Python emitter must recognize the CStrArray shape (name + pointee-is-CString shape + owned field, not just the name) and emit from_list/as_list/free helpers plus an owning-return convert-then-free façade wrapper.
